analysis: The code snippet calls `substring` in multiple places. According to the documentation, `substring` throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException` if `beginIndex` is negative or larger than the length of the string. In each call, the index is derived from `indexOf` which returns -1 when not found, but all calls are guarded by conditions checking that the index is not -1 (e.g., `if (idx > -1)`, `if (redirectUri.indexOf('?') != -1)`, and `if (i >= 0)`). Additionally, the indices are always less than the string length because they represent positions of characters within the string. Therefore, all calls have valid indices, and the exception is avoided in every case.
remark: All substring calls are protected by conditions that ensure the beginIndex is non-negative and within the string length. For example, `validRedirect.substring(0, idx)` is only executed when `idx > -1` (i.e., the string contains '/*'), so idx is between 0 and length-2. Similarly, `redirectUri.substring(0, redirectUri.indexOf('?'))` occurs only when `indexOf('?') != -1`, guaranteeing a valid index. The single-argument `r.substring(i)` is guarded by `if (i >= 0)`, where i is the index of a character found by `indexOf`, so it is always valid. Thus, no `IndexOutOfBoundsException` can occur.
